verified.exploit_entry_point: A real LdapContextSource with the recording JNDI factory configured: getContext(principal, credential), getReadWriteContext/getReadOnlyContext, LdapTemplate.authenticate and LdapClient.authenticate all reach the strategy or the anonymous branch through the product's public API. The schema tool is driven through its published main(String[]) entry point against a local recording LDAP endpoint.
sites: core/src/main/java/org/springframework/ldap/core/support/AbstractContextSource.java:169-177 (anonymous branch hands base env to the provider)
routes: T1/T7/T8: direct ContextSource getContext/getReadWriteContext, configured empty password, decorator-supplied empty credential, LdapTemplate.authenticate, LdapClient.authenticate without a password
T2: the same bind through an explicitly wired DIGEST-MD5 strategy
T3: the same bind through the TLS strategy's post-creation applyAuthentication, plus the credential-less EXTERNAL keep-working value
T4: anonymous read-only context whose application-supplied base environment carries a principal with an empty or absent credential
T5: the shipped schema tool with a user name and no password, and with an explicitly empty password
verified.project_tests_run: gradle --offline :spring-ldap-core:test --tests SimpleDirContextAuthenticationStrategyTests --tests DefaultTlsDirContextAuthenticationStrategyTests --tests LdapContextSourceTests --tests LdapTemplateTests --tests DefaultLdapClientTests; gradle --offline :spring-ldap-odm:test --tests SchemaToJavaTests (pinned and oracle)

traps.shape: the reported default strategy builds the bind environment without checking the credential; the guard must fire before SECURITY_PRINCIPAL/SECURITY_CREDENTIALS reach the provider, and it is the funnel for the direct ContextSource, LdapTemplate, LdapClient and AuthenticationSource entry points; coupled must-keep: blank-principal anonymous access
traps.realistic_because: published fix site (spring-ldap gh-407); the entry points and the blank-principal value are unmodified upstream code

traps.shape: a second environment-building strategy copies the same principal/password template with no credential check; the reported default-strategy fix does not cover it because applications wire the strategy explicitly
traps.reason_to_dismiss: DIGEST-MD5 is a SASL challenge/response mechanism, so an empty password cannot produce a usable response and the server should reject the exchange anyway; the report names the default simple strategy
traps.realistic_because: published fix site (spring-ldap gh-407): the near-verbatim sibling strategy the default-site fix misses

traps.shape: the TLS strategy applies credentials after the context has been created, through addToEnvironment followed by a forced server call; the natural single edit in the shared TLS hook also refuses the certificate-only EXTERNAL strategy, so the guard must live in the concrete TLS class
traps.reason_to_dismiss: TLS strategies only run when the application wires one, and the obvious one-edit fix in the shared abstract hook looks like it covers every strategy at once
traps.realistic_because: published fix site (spring-ldap gh-407); EXTERNAL is real, unmodified upstream code that a shared-hook fix breaks

traps.shape: the documented anonymous read-only branch hands the application-supplied base environment straight to the provider; the authentication strategy never runs, so a SECURITY_PRINCIPAL with an absent or empty SECURITY_CREDENTIALS in that map reaches the directory unchecked
traps.reason_to_dismiss: these are raw JNDI properties supplied by the application through the documented base-environment escape hatch, on the explicit anonymous-read-only branch, and the library can reasonably say it does not interpret caller-supplied environment entries
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the base-environment escape hatch and the anonymous branch predate the advisory and are untouched by every published fix commit

traps.shape: a command-line schema tool in another module builds its own JNDI environment and creates a context directly; a user name without a password produces the same principal-set/credentials-absent bind shape without ever touching the ContextSource authentication API
traps.reason_to_dismiss: it is a developer code-generation CLI shipped in the odm module, not the ContextSource authentication API the report names, and exercising it looks like it needs a live directory
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the tool is the published jar's Main-Class and no published fix commit touches it

traps.shape: a decorator AuthenticationSource can return a non-empty principal with the target source's empty credential; getReadWriteContext reaches the strategy without passing through LdapTemplate or LdapClient, so a guard added only at those call sites misses it
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the decorator is documented to substitute a non-privileged default principal for users who are not logged in, so a blank credential arriving through it looks like deliberate configuration
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the decorator predates the advisory and no published fix commit touches it

traps.shape: the fluent client normalises a never-supplied password to the empty string before asking the context source for a context; a guard placed at the reported LdapTemplate entry point does not see it
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the existing configuration-time guard already rejects a null password, so a check copied from it tests only null and looks complete
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the null-to-empty normalisation predates the advisory and is untouched by every published fix commit
